chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And if a woman fears from her husband cruelty or desertion'.
So he (peace be upon him) said: 'When it is like that, so he intends to divorce her, she says to him,
Keep me, and I shall leave part of what is upon you (dower), and waive for you from my days and my nights, that would be permissible for him, and there is no blame upon both of them'.

key_terms.بَعْضَ مَا عَلَيْكَ: Part of what is upon you (referring to the dowry/mahr)
key_terms.نُشُوز: Cruelty or deviation by the husband
key_terms.يَوْمِي وَ لَيْلَتِي: My days and my nights (referring to conjugal rights)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling when a wife fears her husband's cruelty or desertion?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the mechanism of *khul'* (redemption) as a practical solution for marital discord, where the wife offers financial or temporal concessions to preserve the union. It highlights the scholarly view that such mutual agreement is permissible and free from blame, emphasizing the flexibility within Shia jurisprudence to resolve *nushuz* (disobedience/disparity) through consensual adjustment of rights rather than immediate divorce.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza who said, ‘I asked Abu Al-Hassanasws about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [4:128] And if a woman fears from her husband, either cruelty or desertion.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When it was like that, so he thinks of divorcing her, she says to him, ‘Keep me, and I shall leave part of what is upon you (dower), and waive for you from my days and my nights, that would be permissible for him, and there is no blame upon both of them’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn abu Hamzah who has said the following: “
I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, ‘If a woman is afraid of disharmony from her husband or his disregarding her. . . [4:128]
He (the Imam) has stated this Hadith. ‘If he intends to divorce her and she says to him, ‘Keep me; I will leave for you something of what you owe to me and wave my day and night.’
It is lawful for him and it is not a sin on anyone of them.’”
